## Why it matters

- **First-party validation closes the loop on this morning's teardown capture.** A replication scoring 0.94 PnL correlation is inference; the manager confirming "most of the read is right" upgrades [[2026-11-11-astraeus-hl-vault-reverse-engineering]] from best-anonymous-inference toward ground truth on the strategy family — while leaving the wrong minority unnamed, which is itself informative.
- **"Half the story" is the interesting claim.** If the fills show a mechanical mean-rev ladder but the order flow (queue placement, pacing, sizing vs. book state, adaptation) carries additional edge, the true alpha is partly execution/discretionary — which the backtest's own June gap (manual rescue buys totaling 31% of equity) already hinted at. That reframes the teardown's counterfactual: the manager's defense of his manual interventions may be exactly the half the fills can't show.
- **Skepticism gates:** the owner has obvious incentive to manage perception after being exposed running a decaying short-gamma premium with manual saves — "you only see half the story" is also a classic unfalsifiable defense; anonymous account; the promised thread is unverified at capture; "most of the read is right" specifies neither which parts are wrong nor how wrong.
- **For the user:** reference only — the pending inbox task from the teardown note (act-or-not decision) now stands on a stronger factual base; if the order-flow thread matters for that call, paste the 🧵 or ask and I'll dig it out.
